title: Antitrust Lawyer on NFL Streaming Cost Concerns
summary: Shindor Cantor Lerner Managing Partner Kellie Lerner discusses the rising cost for sports fans to watch their teams through various streaming platforms such as the NFL, and potential legal ramifications for antitrust violations. She speaks to Romaine Bostick on Bloomberg's 'The Close.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Better Home & Finance Founder on Fight for Company
summary: Embattled former Better.com CEO Vishal Garg says he believes that 'the job of making home ownership better for all Americans is not done' after he departed the company on August 3rd. He claims to have the support of a majority of Class A and B shareholders to return to the head of the company, in lieu of interim CEO Daniel Lewis. He speaks to Romaine Bostick on Bloomberg's 'The Close.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Aston Martin CEO on new luxury model, the Valen
summary: Aston Martin CEO Adrian Hallmark speaks to Romaine Bostick on Bloomberg's 'The Close' about the company's newest model, the Valen. More powerful than any other front-engine vehicle in its 113-year history and capped at 150 cars worldwide, Hallmark details what makes this model different from any other. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Former Boston Fed Pres.: Investment spend a catalyst
summary: Former Boston Federal Reserve President Eric Rosengren isn't surprised by a weaker retail sales number with the American consumer dealing with higher oil prices while AI and tech investment drive a large portion of investment spending. He speaks to Romaine Bostick and Isabelle Lee on Bloomberg's 'The Close.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hollywood Box Offices Are Back
summary: Hollywood has once again cheated death. The first seven-plus months of 2026 have revived the industry’s faith — not just in movies but in the act of going to the theater. Global ticket sales have increased 15% from a year earlier and are on pace for their best annual total since 2019. Five movies have eclipsed $1 billion, with Spider-Man: Brand New Day almost clearing that on opening weekend. With new installments of Dune and Avengers coming, that group could swell to seven — the second-most on record. Bloomberg News Media & Entertainment Managing Editor Lucas Shaw brings us the latest from Hollywood.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: FBI Epstein Emails Show Sarah Ferguson Reached Patel
summary: Bloomberg News Senior Investigative Reporter writes a weekly newsletter, The FOIA Files. This week's edition show "records, which include emails, spreadsheets and training slides, provide a window into the internal deliberations at the highest levels of government as officials discussed how to review, redact and release the Epstein files." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Lula’s Lead Over Bolsonaro Narrows in Brazil Election Poll
summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s lead over right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro narrowed ahead of Brazil’s October presidential election, according to a new poll published Friday.

title: Volatile Week for Equity Markets | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Katie Greifeld, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Berkshire Pads Delta, Alphabet Stakes as Abel Taps Cash Pile
summary: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. increased its holdings in Delta Air Lines Inc. and Google parent Alphabet Inc. as Greg Abel began tapping into the company’s massive cash hoard.

title: Election Angst Fuels Bruising Week in Brazil Markets
summary: Brazilian assets posted some of the biggest losses in the world this week amid growing angst over the October presidential election.

title: EM Currencies Cap Best Streak Since 2024, Stocks Rebound on AI
summary: Emerging-market assets rose on Friday as a shift in the US interest-rate outlook added to bullish sentiment around artificial intelligence, pushing equities to cap the best week in nearly two months and sending a gauge of currencies on the longest streak of gains since 2024.

title: US Stocks End Off Record Highs to Mark Third Week of Gains
summary: US equities ended with gains for a third straight week, their longest winning streak since May, even as they slipped off record highs on Friday after softer consumer data.

title: Understanding Hyperscalers | Masters in Business with Ankur Crawford
summary: Ankur Crawford, Executive Vice President and Portfolio Manager of the Alger Capital Appreciation, Alger Focus Equity, and Alger Spectra Strategies joins Barry for a conversation about how she builds an investment strategy. They also discuss her journey from engineering to investment, along with understanding AI and compute investment cycles.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Avoid Being Shaken Out Of The Market: Wilson
summary: Mike Wilson, chief US equity strategist & chief investment officer at Morgan Stanley, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Freshmen Pay Thousands For Sorority Rush Coaches
summary: Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how young women rushing sororities have been paying from $3K to $12K for coaches to teach them southern sororities unwritten rules in hopes of getting accepted. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Nears $4,400 as Traders Weigh Fed Interest-Rate Path
summary: Gold edged toward $4,400 an ounce as traders weighed the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path after the economy’s main engine showed signs of cooling.

title: Gen Z Moves Money From Stocks to Sports Bets
summary:
Bloomberg's Zijia Song joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Sports betting is increasingly competing with traditional investing for younger Americans’ attention, with more than a quarter of Gen Z investors saying they see gambling on sports as part of their long-term financial strategy, according to a survey by personal finance platform Betterment.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hedge Funds Halved Short Bets on Yen Since Joint Intervention
summary: Hedge funds further dialed back on their wagers against the yen, signaling a reduction in negative sentiment surrounding the currency after the US and Japan’s historic joint intervention.

title: Leveraged ETFs Snap Back as Casino Crowd Mints $50 Billion
summary: Three weeks ago, Wall Street’s casino crowd took a beating. AI stocks buckled, semiconductor shares tumbled and leveraged trades unraveled.

title: 'Field of Dreams,' 'Bronx is Burning': Must-Read Baseball Books
summary:
Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene discuss their must-read book on this weeks edition of "Bloomberg Money." They discuss "Shoeless Joe: The Inspiration for Field of Dreams" by W. P. Kinsella and "Ladies and Gentlemen, the Bronx Is Burning: 1977, Baseball, Politics, and the Battle for the Soul of a City" by Jonathan Mahler.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
